chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him)

key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Like it / The same (referring to a previous narration)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'mithluhu' indicate in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the authenticity of the preceding hadith by attributing it to Musa ibn Ja'far (al-Kazim), a key link in the chain of transmission for Imami jurisprudence. It underscores the scholarly rigor of the *Tahdhib* in preserving identical reports to reinforce the legal weight of testifying to a will (*al-ishaad ala al-wasiyyah*). This repetition highlights the importance of clear witness testimony in ensuring the faithful execution of an Imam’s or individual’s final directives.
